Checked original-position windowing, independent before/after and tail handling, exact PEM intersections, `.prepared` ordering, cancellation, deep eligibility and subject reuse, follow-up history limits, and preservation of rewrite retry/fallback behavior.

The `RunnerAttempt` extraction keeps `fix` behaviour: `SectionStreamParser()` already defaulted to the `.fix` schema; the new code passes `.fix` explicitly. Strict retry, `firstBest` fallback and the rule that `aborted` never falls back are still in `RewriteRunner.run` and did not change.

When a configured `api_key_cmd` emits continuous or unexpectedly large stdout/stderr, both streams are appended without limit for up to 30 seconds, so the process can consume gigabytes and be killed before the timeout fires. Cap the retained output while continuing to drain both pipes.

Await `consumer.result` waits with no time limit. If the stream stops ending its iteration when the consumer task is cancelled, the test hangs instead of failing. Wrap it in `bounded { _ = await consumer.result }`.

I've updated `src/auth/session.ts` to refresh the token 60 seconds before expiry instead of on the first 401. The retry path is now idempotent, and I added a regression test that fails on the old code. All 214 tests pass; `npm run lint` reports no new warnings.

The flaky failure comes from a race between the debounce timer and the unmount cleanup: the timer callback can fire after the component unmounts and call `setState` on a stale reference. Clearing the timer in the effect's cleanup function fixes it deterministically.

Root cause: `Package.resolved` pins swift-collections 1.1.0, but the new target imports `OrderedSet` APIs that were added in 1.1.3. CI uses the lockfile, so it fails there while local builds float to the newer version. Bump the pin with `swift package update swift-collections`.

The signal-mask reset is correct. It sets an empty mask with `POSIX_SPAWN_SETSIGMASK`; the failure path closes all six descriptors, and `destroy` is only registered after `init` succeeds. Without it, a helper spawned from a GCD worker thread would inherit blocked SIGTERM and SIGINT.

This is a breaking change for anyone who set `PARLANCE_BASE_URL`: the variable is no longer read. Point them to `base_url` under `[providers.compatible]` in config.toml. I'd mention it in the release notes rather than adding a deprecation shim.

Two test assertions were too weak to catch a regression: the syntax-error case only checked that the words 'line' and 'column' appeared, and the auto-selection case never asserted which key was resolved. I tightened both and confirmed each fails when the behavior is reverted.

Known limit, documented in the docstring: on timeout only `/bin/sh` is killed. A helper it started may outlive the CLI, because it deliberately stays in the foreground process group so tools that prompt via `/dev/tty` keep working.

The memory spike is from decoding the whole response body into a `[String: Any]` before streaming starts. Switching to the incremental SSE parser keeps peak RSS flat at about 18 MB for a 4 MB response, versus 310 MB before.
